datasheet.title: 7280R3 Series Data Center Switch Router Data Sheet (Arista Networks, 03-0045-59, August 11th, 2025)

description: Arista 7280CR3-32D4 - a fixed 1RU data-centre switch router with 32 x 100G QSFP ports and 4 x 400G QSFP-DD ports, running EOS. The front carries the 100G cages in two stacked rows, the odd number on top, in two blocks of eight columns. The four 400G cages are two stacked columns between the blocks. Each port has a status lamp. Four system lamps (system, fan, PS1, PS2) are at the right. The rear carries two hot-swap power supplies at the ends and three hot-swap fan modules. It also carries the RJ-45 management port, the USB port and the RJ-45 console port. The same panel is ordered with front-to-rear air (-F) or rear-to-front air (-R). It is sold as the 7280CR3, as the 7280CR3K with more memory and routes, and as the 7280CR3K-32D4A with an eight-core CPU.

gaps.note: The 7280CR3K-32D4A draws 543 W typical and 865 W maximum (guide Table 4) against 535 W and 851 W for the other two, has an eight-core CPU in place of a quad-core, and the K builds carry 64 GB of memory against 8 GB. No configuration can state a device attribute (the same open gap as cisco/asr-9001). The attrs carry the 7280CR3-32D4's figures and the platform lines name all three.

Storage temperature -25 to 70 C (guide Table 2) against -40 to 70 C (data sheet), and relative humidity 5 to 90 percent against 5 to 95 percent. The guide's, the newer document by three months, are in attrs.
gaps.wanted: the maker's statement of which is current.

gaps.note: The PWR-1011-DC input is "-40 to -60 VDC, 30 A" in guide Table 3 and "-48 to -60V DC" in the data sheet's power supply table. The guide's is in the component, the data sheet's in its provenance.
gaps.wanted: the maker's statement of which is current.

gaps.note: The guide's Figures 3-1 to 3-4 are isometric drawings of another switch and carry no measure, and the kit guides for KIT-7001, KIT-7101-D and the other spares are not held, so no ear position or rail kit is written.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned drawing of the mounting bracket position, and the kit guides.

gaps.note: Figure C-4 draws a pair of dots a port, but Table 10 describes one port LED and does not say what the second lamp of the pair shows. Both are given Table 10's states.
gaps.wanted: the guide's account of the two port lamps, or a photograph of the lit face.

gaps.note: The port-speed strips' legends, the small print over each cage, the system and fan lamp glyphs and the PS1 and PS2 legends are unreadable in the 575 px figure. The glyphs and the two PS legends are drawn as read; the strip and cage legends are not drawn.
Which side the latches of the stacked cages face is not visible in the figure. The library's belly-to-belly convention is used (upper cage upright, lower turned 180).
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the stacked cages.

gaps.note: The management block's two arrow marks and its console symbol (a small outlined box with three ticks, as the figure draws it; the figure does not resolve it further) are drawn as read; the order of the three ports (management over USB over console) follows the datasheet's rear view and the library's other Arista stacks, and the figure's 1.24 px/mm resolves it only as three stacked ports. The lamps on the management jack are the library's single Ethernet jack's.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the rear management block.

gaps.note: The PWR-1011-DC supplies are drawn as the AC supply's housing with a plain two-pole terminal block. The guide shows a DC supply only in the isometric Figures 4-5 and 4-7, with a red terminal cover and the protective-earth terminal on the far side; the real terminal arrangement is not drawn.
gaps.wanted: a flat drawing or photograph of the PWR-1011-DC.

gaps.note: The guide's power tables and the data sheet give whole-switch figures only; the fan modules' missing power figure (lint L27) stands. The supplies state their output.
The 1RU grounding point is on the bottom of the chassis for KIT-GND-EXT-1RU (guide section 4.2, Table 5, Figure 4-2). No flat figure measures it, so it is not placed.
gaps.wanted: a flat drawing of the bottom with the grounding bracket holes.

name: 7280cr3-32d4

chassis.note: Guide Table 1: 48.3 x 4.4 x 55.8 cm (19 x 1.75 x 22.0 in), 12.3 kg (27.0 lbs), the same for the 7280CR3-32D4, 7280CR3K-32D4 and 7280CR3K-32D4A. Data sheet: 43.99 x 4.37 x 55.83 cm (17.3 x 1.72 x 22.0 in), 27 lbs (12.27 kg). The width: 48.3 cm is over the mounting ears, so the body between them, which is what is modelled, is the data sheet's 43.99 cm (440.0 here), a 21.5 mm ear each side. The height is the data sheet's 43.7 (the guide rounds it to 4.4 cm). The depth is the data sheet's 558.3 (the guide's 55.8 cm is the same figure rounded). 1RU.

colour.note: The front plate is the median of bare-plate pixels in the guide's figure C-4, #aaabad.

configurations.note: Data sheet ordering information: DCS-7280CR3-32D4-F and -R, DCS-7280CR3K-32D4-F and -R, and DCS-7280CR3K-32D4A-F and -R ("front to rear air, 2 x AC" and "rear to front air, 2 x AC"). The "#" SKUs ("configurable fans and psu") and DCS-7280CR3-32D4-M# are orders of parts, not part numbers a DCIM can hold, and are not listed. The data sheet lists no DC build of the switch: the PWR-1011-DC-RED and -BLUE supplies are spares, so the DC configurations are examples with no part number. The K and K-A builds share the base model's size, weight, figure and supplies and differ in memory, CPU, routes and (for the -A) power draw, which a configuration cannot state; each is a configuration with its own part numbers. There is no empty-bay (-S) configuration: no -S suffix exists in this family and the guide draws no blank for a power supply or fan module.

ears.note: NOT MODELLED. The guide's Chapter 3 mounts the switch with the accessory-kit brackets and shows them in Figures 3-1 to 3-4, isometric drawings of a different switch ("Illustrations in this chapter depict the mounting of a DCS-7050QX-32S switch") that carry no measure. The data sheet lists the spares KIT-7001, KIT-2POST-1U-NT, KIT-4POST-NT, KIT-7001-4POST-L, KIT-7101-D, KIT-7101-RK and KIT-7101-LD-RK. The guide says a four-post mount is recommended and a two-post mount is centre-mount only. No figure measures a bracket position, and the kit guides are not held, so no ear position is written and no rail kit is listed in chassis.kits. Recorded in the gap rack-ears.

environment.note: Guide Table 2: operating 0 to 40 C, storage -25 to 70 C, altitude 0 to 3,000 m, humidity 5 to 90 percent non-condensing. Data sheet: operating 0 to 40 C, storage -40 to 70 C, humidity 5 to 95 percent, altitude 0 to 3,000 m. Storage temperature and humidity differ: gap `environment`, the guide's used.

front-legend.note: The vertical model legend reads "7280CR3-32D4" up the left plate (centre 26.1 mm down, baseline 4.6 mm across) with the maker's wordmark above the first column from 2.6 to 16.7 mm across and 9.4 to 11.8 down. THE WORDMARK IS NOT DRAWN: a logo-zone region is reserved over it and the plain model text is set. The figure prints "7280CR3-32D4" on the plate in blue; its small print is not legible, so the text is as the guide's caption names the model.

front-ports.note: Figure C-4 at 1.273 px/mm anchored on the 440 mm body, read in a three-times enlargement. Thirty-two QSFP100 cages in two stacked rows (ports 1 to 32), in eight-column blocks of two groups of four columns: ports 1 to 16 and 17 to 32. The white number tabs read, for the top row, 1, 3, 5, 7 at 24.0, 43.2, 62.4 and 81.7 mm, 9, 11, 13, 15 at 113.6 to 170.9, then 17 to 23 at 267.1 to 324.0 and 25 to 31 at 356.1 to 413.1. The column pitch inside a group is 19.1 (the registry's 19.0 ganged-QSFP pitch) and the gap between the groups is 13.6 (ports 7 to 9) and 13.0 (ports 23 to 25) mm wider than a column. Two stacked 400G QSFP-DD cages (33 over 34 at 201.1 mm, 35 over 36 at 236.7 mm) sit between the blocks, which put the 400G columns 30.2 and 30.4 mm from their neighbours. The yellow boxes of the figure enclose both rows at 12.2 to 37.3 mm down, so the openings are read at 12.4 (upper) and 27.7 to 37.3 (lower) mm: a row pitch of 15.3 mm, the figure's tab centres reading 15.7. The belly-to-belly orientation is the library's convention (upper cage upright, lower turned 180); the figure is too small to show the latch side.

fru-bays.note: Guide Appendix E (E.2 power supplies, E.3 fan modules) gives removal and installation procedures, and the data sheet calls the supplies "1+1 hot-swappable" and the fans "hot-swap". SO THE TWO POWER SUPPLIES AND THE THREE FAN MODULES ARE BAYS. Nothing on this chassis is a built-in unit. The management block, the USB port and the console port are part of the chassis and are placements.

gate-1-front.note: Figure C-4 passes at 1.0 percent. The raster is 575 x 116 pixels. The body between its edges measures 560 px wide and 55.6 px tall (aspect 10.07), against the data sheet's 440.0 / 43.7 = 10.07, so the figure is near-orthographic and carries geometry at 1.273 px/mm (the 440 mm body is the scale anchor). One pixel is 0.79 mm, so every front position is good to about 0.8 mm, and every one is `estimated` because it is read off a picture and no dimension states it. The cage columns were read from the white port-number tabs in a three-times enlargement.

gate-1-rear.note: Figure D-2 passes at 1.6 percent: the raster is 552 px wide, the chassis 545 px between its edges (1.239 px/mm over the 440 mm body) and 55 px tall (44.4 mm against 43.7). Positions are measures off the figure, good to about 0.8 mm. The guide draws the rear generically (D-1 to D-4) and does not say which model uses which. The 7280CR3-32D4 is mapped to D-2 by its three fan modules (data sheet: "Hot-swappable Fans 3 (N+1 redundant)"), its 1RU height, its two power supplies, and its management ports at the rear (Figure C-4 has none at the front). THE MAPPING IS ESTIMATED.

interface-names.note: Not printed and not modelled. EOS names ports Ethernet1 to Ethernet36 and Management1; this is the vendor's convention and no held document prints it.

lifecycle.note: Searched 2026-10-22 for an end-of-sale notice for the 7280CR3-32D4, 7280CR3K-32D4 and 7280CR3K-32D4A on Arista's advisories and notices pages. The searches found notices for the 7280CR2A and 7280CR2K series and for select 7280CR models (advisories 15849, 15850 and 16536) and none for these models.

other-faces.note: No source draws the top, bottom or sides flat. The guide's installation figures are isometric. Each carries an `empty` sentence. The 1RU grounding point is on the bottom of the chassis (guide section 4.2, Table 5, KIT-GND-EXT-1RU); no figure measures it.

port-lamps.note: Guide Appendix A.1.2, Table 10: "Port LEDs near their corresponding ports provide a link and operational status": off the link is down, green link up, yellow software disabled, flashing yellow failed diagnostics. Figure C-4 draws a pair of small dark dots above each upper cage column and below each lower one (the guide's Figure A-3 captions them "Port 4 LEDs"). TWO LAMPS A PORT are modelled, a and b, centred on the column and 2.0 mm apart (the figure's dots sit nearer, about 1.5 mm, but two 2.0 mm holes cannot overlap), and the 400G cages carry the same pair. Table 10 gives one set of states, so both lamps carry it; what each of the two means is the gap port-lamp-count.

port-numbering.note: Figure C-4 (callout 5, "Port numbers") prints 1 over 2, 3 over 4, and so on down each column and across, 1 to 32 in the two blocks, then 33 over 34 and 35 over 36 in the 400G columns, which sit between ports 15 and 17 in space but are numbered after 32. The odd number is the upper cage. The figure prints each number on a white tab over the cage opening; a seated cage hides what is painted under it, so the numerals are set above each upper cage and below each lower one, in the band the lamps share. EOS interface names are not printed on the metal and are not modelled.

power.note: Guide Table 4: typical / maximum 535 W / 851 W for the 7280CR3-32D4 and 7280CR3K-32D4, and 543 W / 865 W for the 7280CR3K-32D4A, each with PWR-1011-AC or PWR-1011-DC. The data sheet states the same figures with typical "measured at 25C ambient with 50% load on all ports". A configuration cannot state a device attribute, so the device carries 535 W / 851 W and the -A figure is in the gap config-scoped-device-attrs and in the description of its configurations.

rear.note: Figure D-2 at 1.239 px/mm, the rear seen from behind with x = 0 at the left of the drawing. PS1 is the left and PS2 the right (callouts 1 and 10). Each power supply module is 73.5 mm wide (the data sheet's "73.5MM") at 4.0 and 362.3 mm across and 1.85 mm down. The management block is a grey plate 83.0 to 101.0 mm across with the Ethernet management port, the USB port and the RJ-45 console port stacked in it in the order the library draws other Arista management stacks. Three fan modules 78.6 mm wide at 107.7, 191.0 and 274.3 mm across (an 83.3 mm pitch) and 2.55 mm down. The figure also draws, between the fans, three release sliders and three lamps, which are in the fan component.

rear-fan.note: Data sheet: "Hot-swappable Fans 3 (N+1 redundant)", "Fan Tray FAN-7011H", FAN-7011H-F (front-to-rear) and FAN-7011H-R (rear-to-front) as spares. Guide section 2.1: a red handle is an air-exit module and a blue handle an air-inlet one, and every module must have the same direction. The three fan modules are bays that accept FAN-7011H-F or -R; the -R configurations seat the blue modules.

sources.note: 7280R3 Series Quick Start Guide, Arista Networks, document DOC-07041-01, 63 pages, PDF created 2025-05-16 (https://www.arista.com/assets/data/pdf/qsg/qsg-books/QS_7280R3.pdf): Table 1 (dimensions and weights), Table 2 (operating and storage), Table 3 (power input), Table 4 (power draw and supported supplies), section 2.1 (airflow orientation, handle colour), section 4.1 and Table 5 (grounding), section 4.5 and Figure 4-9 (serial and management ports), Appendix A (status indicators, Tables 9 to 13), Appendix B (parts list), Appendix C (Figure C-4, the front panel of the DCS-7280CR3-32D4, 7280CR3K-32D4 and 7280CR3K-32D4A), Appendix D (Figure D-2, the rear panel with three fan modules), Appendix E (field replacement of power supplies and fan modules). 7280 Data Center Switches Quick Start Guide, Arista Networks, 58 pages, PDF created 2022-06-03 (https://www.arista.com/assets/data/pdf/qsg/qsg-books/QS_7280_1RU_Gen3.pdf): Figure 48 (DCS-7280CR3-32D4 and 7280CR3K-32D4), which is the same 574 x 116 pixel raster as Figure C-4 (compared pixel for pixel: identical), so it is a repeat of the source and not a second reading. 7280R3 Series Data Center Switch Router Data Sheet, Arista Networks, 03-0045-59, dated August 11th, 2025 (https://www.arista.com/assets/data/pdf/Datasheets/7280R3-Data-Sheet.pdf): the model comparison table of the 7280CR3-32D4, 7280CR3K-32D4 and 7280CR3K-32D4A, the power supply specifications, and the ordering information. Held and checked first: intake COVERAGE.md and SOURCES.md, which list no photograph, Visio stencil, 3D model or CAD file for this model (Arista publishes none; the stencil zip could not be fetched). The data sheet's picture of the face is a 396 x 39 pixel strip and the guide's Figure C-4 a 575 x 116 pixel raster; both are low resolution. No drawing, photograph or logo is copied into the library, only transcribed facts and new drawings.

speed-strips.note: Guide Figure C-4 callout 6, "Port-speed group", draws a lavender strip between the two rows under each four-column group of 100G cages and an orange strip under the two 400G columns. The strips are drawn in those colours at 23.8 to 26.0 mm down. Their printed legends are unreadable and are not drawn.

status-lamps.note: Guide Appendix A.1.1, Table 9 and Figure C-4 callouts 1 to 4: a system status lamp (blinking green on power-up, green normal, blue locator, amber for two or more failed fans), a fan status lamp (green, amber for one module removed or failed, red for two or more) and a status lamp for each of the two power supplies (green operating, off removed or faulty). Four lamps in a column at 431.1 mm, 11.2, 14.5, 17.8 and 21.1 mm down, in a rounded plate 429.0 to 437.2 mm across and 9.0 to 24.3 down. The printed glyphs are a system symbol, a fan symbol and two small legends read as PS1 and PS2.

vents.note: The figure shows a perforated strip along the top (1.0 to 5.1 mm down, across nearly the whole width), grids of dark square vents in the gaps between the port groups (92.8 to 102.4, 182.4 to 189.8, 213.8 to 224.2, 248.4 to 255.6 and 335.4 to 344.8 mm across, 9.6 to 39.6 down), two small grids left of port 1, a column and a three-by-three grid right of port 31, and a row of squares along the bottom lip. Each is drawn as a vent field in its measured extent; the individual squares are not drawn one by one.
